newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Tung to visit Beijing for committee finale.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung to visit Beijing for committee finale.

text.p: Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa will visit Beijing on Friday for the swansong of the committee which laid the groundwork for the territory's government under Chinese rule, Tung's office said on Thursday.
"He's going up there as a deputy director of the committee and to wind it up because this is the last session," a Tung spokesman told Reuters.

China's parliament last week approved the scrapping of the Preparatory Committee, a 150-member body of Chinese communist officials and Hong Kong notables created to pave the way for the former British colony's transition to Chinese rule on July 1.
The committee chose a 400-member caucus that picked Tung as post-handover chief executive and appointed the controversial Provisional Legislature last December.
The committee is due to announce its demise at the final plenum on Friday.
Tung, on his first visit to Beijing since he took office, had no events planned with Chinese officials other than the final committee session and a banquet afterwards, the spokesman said.
"There's no other official meeting scheduled," he said. "He'll probably meet some people at lunch on Saturday."
Tung plans to throw himself into governing Hong Kong after he returns on Saturday evening, the spokesman said.

"He'd like to get down to running the joint because we've had so many official functions in the last 10 days," he said. "As he said himself, he'd like to get a bit of sleep and then get back to the ordinary running of Hong Kong."
Tung has been in the spotlight with a demanding schedule of social and diplomatic functions since he took the reins of the thriving territory from outgoing colonial governor Chris Patten.
"It has been a very busy time but I think what he has mainly in mind is to settle down and get ready for his policy speech (to the territory) in October," the spokesman said.
With the Preparatory Committee set for its final session, another China-backed body was getting ready to oversee Hong Kong affairs.
Beijing said last week it had created a committee to monitor the Basic Law, the territory's post-handover mini-constitution, with six members from Hong Kong and six from China.
